For d=3 the probability that coordinate i wins is (2/π) arctan(w_i/q) with q=sqrt(w1w2+w1w3+w2w3), obtained by the two opposite rectangular-cone solid angles. Its derivative is arctan(w_i/q)/(πw_i), strictly decreasing in w_i at fixed q, proving Schur concavity via pair balancing and continuity to the closed simplex; the planar edge case follows likewise. The d≥4 violation uses a=(1/3,1/3,1/3,0...), b=(8/25,8/25,8/25,1/25,0...); a majorizes b but F(b)-F(a)≤0.5 log(24/25)+1/(6√2π²)=-0.008470181254903494...<0. The bound follows from an exact t³ small-ball estimate and E|Z|³; mixing both weights with uniform positive weights preserves the strict reversal. This is not inferred from finite quadrature or the packaged VERIFY_OK claim.
